central_question: Can a WAM use its own imagined action-future pairs to decide both when extra test-time sampling is warranted and which sampled rollout should be executed, without task labels or a learned value head?
argument_chain: A WAM rollout exposes an action chunk plus multi-view future images.
The action-future gate cheaply tests whether projected end-effector motion agrees with image optical flow.
If inconsistent, sample up to Nmax candidates and score frozen-model cross-view depth reprojection consistency.
Execute the minimum-error candidate; evaluate fixed-budget gains, selective-compute recovery, selector diagnostics, and large-N failures.
required_quantitative_evidence: Table 1 five headline settings and paired confidence intervals, including X-WAM Door/Drawer 96.7 to 92.1 exception
Table 2 Nmax=8 mean 74.8% recovery and 26.2% trigger; ranges 63.6-85.7 and 14.2-34.5
Table 3 offline ER versus online success and proxy boundary
Table 5 GeoBoN versus Cosmos Policy value head
Figure 2 false low-score rates 7/10/12/32% for N=2/4/8/16
evidence_boundaries: simulation only; no physical robot evidence
training-free does not mean inference-free or cost-free
paired 95% CI calculation method is unspecified
consensus baseline is a reimplementation because original code is unavailable
offline ER is only a proxy and is not equivalent to online closed-loop success
selector outliers cause non-monotonic scaling with candidate count
no appendix, algorithm block, or dedicated limitations/acknowledgments/availability/impact/ethics section
